It aims to bring the device to market within the next two to three years. The device will launch first in China before potentially expanding to the US. BrainCo currently markets brain-computer interface-enabled headsets to address neurological disorders such as autism, ADHD, and insomnia. Its devices can collect, decode, and stimulate neural signals.

tech.title: How software engineering is changing: a tale of two eras
tech.summary: AI-native startups can ship even faster than fast-moving pre-AI startups because they risk nothing by moving too fast. The old constraints of software engineering have disappeared, allowing startups to move faster, but also break things. The new constraints are too much context switching, losing shared context, tougher pacing, less focus on design, and AI plan limits. Many existing technologies and processes will crack under the change.

tech.title: Interpolative Software
tech.summary: Interpolative software is code that is solidly within the training distribution of models. It can often be specified with just a few sentences of prompting. Novel software is something that has fundamentally not existed before. Writing novel software with agents is challenging, as they are not trained on the task. Not a lot of software is novel, which is fine, as there is still a ton of value in the interpolative stuff.

tech.title: The Death of the Angel Investor
tech.summary: The economics of angel investing have shifted. Many investors have realized it's potentially more profitable to raise a fund instead of using their own money. Technology startups now move much faster, and running around grabbing small checks from angels is less palatable than grabbing a pre-seed fund to fund a whole initial round. Also, when angels try to fund a round, they are often pushed out by the valuation game.

This study looks at how models trained on the architecture perform when trained for longer as a pressure test along the way towards larger models and video. Examples of images generated by the resulting model are available.

QEMU emulation exposed how a script parser's file writes and Linux's core-dump handling could combine into code execution. The eventual fix changed the stored GPS time offset from 180 minutes to 120.

webdev.title: The hidden latency inside your database
webdev.summary: Network-attached storage adds latency inside a database cluster, even when the application and database are close together. Local NVMe avoids that hop, but requires deliberate replication and failover to preserve durability. Workloads that fit mostly in RAM may see little benefit, while frequent cache misses and IOPS limits make storage placement worth examining.

webdev.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI
webdev.summary: OpenAI built Pando, a Git-compatible backend that handles pushes to unrelated branches independently and reuses cached packfiles across fetches. It reduced median push latency by nearly 80% and now serves nearly a petabyte of Git data per day. The tradeoff is weaker consistency across branches and some redundant downloads, allowing writes to scale horizontally and reads to saturate clients' network connections.

webdev.title: Resisting Cognitive Surrender
webdev.summary: Uncritically accepting agent output can increase technical debt while eroding the understanding needed to debug and maintain a system. Choose how much to delegate based on risk, stay involved in consequential decisions, and ask for small, comprehensible changes. When delegating more fully, use independent observability, deterministic checks, and shadow traffic to verify behavior rather than relying solely on the agent's account.

webdev.title: Auditioning Engineering: Software Engineering Interviews in the Age of AI
webdev.summary: Warner Music Group encourages candidates to use AI while solving realistic API integration problems against a live, randomized test server. Its system-design interview asks candidates to modify an existing system and infer causes from observed behavior. The approach emphasizes technical judgment, although building new coding exercises and training senior system-design interviewers remain costly.

webdev.title: The weight-space programming post is misleading
webdev.summary: This critique separates experiments that inspect small networks' raw weights from larger-model experiments that use Python and execution feedback. The Qwen result involved 50 batches of practice problems, so it does not demonstrate improvement from inspecting raw weights alone. The distinction matters when judging whether the work shows one general capability or several different engineering techniques.

It keeps the entire VM state in one byte array, allowing execution to pause between instructions, snapshot while waiting for tools, and resume elsewhere. The focused runtime deliberately omits features such as ES modules, Intl, and a JIT.

Editing 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights reduced reasoning loops and raised MATH-500 accuracy from 7.9% to 48.1% with 50 forward passes for feedback. The gains removed an obstacle to existing ability, while similar edits failed to meaningfully improve a Gemma model that rarely looped.

webdev.title: Could a modern chess engine on a Pentium have defeated Kasparov in 1996?

infosec.title: Financial Services Firm MoneySmart Hit By IT Security Breach, Some Customers' Data Copied
infosec.summary: Financial services company MoneySmart disclosed that a “security incident” led to the disclosure of some of its customers' personal data in Hong Kong and Singapore. MoneySmart said the data may include names and email addresses, shipping addresses, and application or policy reference numbers for customers who submitted rewards claims.

infosec.title: Prioritize What Attackers Will Exploit: 4 Elements of Strong Exposure Prioritization
infosec.summary: Fewer than 10% of vulnerabilities are exploited, but remediation programs often treat most findings as urgent. Rank exposures using active-exploitation intelligence, asset criticality, EPSS-style exploitability modeling, and control validation. A vulnerability on an internet-facing system that handles regulated data, has known exploitation, and lacks segmentation should outrank a high-CVSS finding on an isolated internal asset. The model measures success by fewer exploitable exposures and reduced remediation effort, rather than ticket volume.

infosec.title: The Quiet Phase: Why Active Directory Group Enumeration Deserves Your Attention
infosec.summary: Attackers map who sits in Domain Admins with SharpHound or PowerView long before they change any group membership, and an audit entry (SACL) on the group's member attribute turns those reads into Event 4662, or 4799 for built-in groups, on the domain controller that answered. On real privileged groups, the signal drowns in reads from directory sync, Exchange, and admin tooling, and SAMR-based tools like net group /domain bypass it entirely. Pair the audit with decoy groups that nothing legitimate ever reads, correlate a decoy read and a real admin-group read from the same logon session, and check coverage with its QuietPhase PowerShell script.

infosec.title: Jailbreaking my car's navigation system just so I can change the time
infosec.summary: A Renault Latitude's TomTom Carminat LIVE head unit hid its clock settings behind a legitimate navigation SD card. The card used CID-based DRM and signed files, so a blank card could not supply the missing menu definition. The author reverse-engineered the Linux 2.6.28 firmware, built a QEMU and CAN emulator, and found that master.script allowed a root path-traversal write through its LOG command and wrote |/bin/sh /media/sdcard/payload.sh into /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern, then crashed /bin/dbus-monitor to trigger a coredump and execute the payload as root. The exploit enabled an eMMC backup and a timezone patch from UTC+3 to UTC+2.

infosec.title: Secure cloud AI with stronger GRC
infosec.summary: Watch this on-demand security demo from AWS and SANS Institute to see how governance, risk, and compliance strategies can help address risk across identity, data, APIs, and agentic workflows. Learn approaches for access control, data protection, and visibility. Watch now and explore AWS Partner solutions in AWS Marketplace.

infosec.title: dragon-tales
infosec.summary: dragon-tales is a binary analysis library for disassembling, assembling, and analyzing machine code across multiple architectures.

infosec.title: Crashtest
infosec.summary: Crashtest runs adversarial security tests against a JavaScript app's real route handlers entirely in-process, so it never opens a socket or needs a live server. Its built-in campaigns cover identity-spoofing headers, prototype pollution, cross-tenant ID enumeration, leaked secrets, and cost-amplification abuse, and every attack ends in a verdict of REFUSED, EXPLOITED, or BOUNDED (an accepted risk with a named owner). It plugs into Hono, Express, and Fastify, and its GitHub Action fails CI only on a new exploit or a regression, never on risks the team already accepted.

infosec.title: safeagents
infosec.summary: safeagents is a local proxy that sits between a coding agent and its model API and checks each tool call before the harness runs it. It blocks calls to undeclared tools and calls that reach hosts nobody mentioned in the conversation, and it runs atif-scan detectors that catch reads of /proc/1/environ or curl --noproxy. Ambiguous calls can go to an optional judge model that sees only the user's prompt, the call, and the findings, never the agent's reasoning, and it works with any harness that accepts a custom base URL, including Claude Code, OpenCode, and Hermes.

infosec.title: Red Hat Patches 9.8-Rated Linux TCP RCE Flaw While Ubuntu Releases Fixes for Testing
infosec.summary: Red Hat has patched CVE-2026-98432, a 9.8-rated use-after-free in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP handling. A remote attacker can send IPv4 Record Route or Timestamp options to a listening TCP port and trigger a race that reads freed memory, potentially allowing code execution. RHEL 8, 9, and 10 fixes require a reboot. No exploitation has been reported. An nftables rule can drop IPv4 TCP packets with IP options, but it does not fully prevent exploitation.

infosec.title: How Cisco defends at machine speed with OpenAI
infosec.summary: Cisco is pairing its network telemetry with OpenAI's Daybreak program and GPT-6 Astra to link signals that look harmless on their own and to speed up vulnerability patching, and Cisco's Jeetu Patel calls the gains "step function improvements." Patel also argued that agent security will depend on telling a hijacked agent apart from one pursuing a legitimate goal in an unintended way. That will take security telemetry and observability data read side by side. The post is an OpenAI customer story with no metrics or technical detail behind its claims, so it reads more as a sign of where vendor AI partnerships are heading than as evidence of results.

infosec.title: Token thieves costing companies $100K+ per day in illicit LLM charges
infosec.summary: Google Mandiant reports that criminals are stealing LLM API keys and cloud service account credentials, then running high-volume model inference at victims' expense. Charges reached $100,000 per day in one case and $1 million in total before access was revoked. One service, Jet Night, allegedly used stolen keys to offer access to frontier models for about $60 per month.

design.title: Nubank unveils global brand refresh by Koto ahead of US launch
design.summary: Koto has refreshed Nubank's global identity ahead of its US expansion, creating a flexible brand system designed to accommodate more than 140 million customers and an expanding portfolio of financial products. The redesign retains the recognizable Nu logo while refining its signature purple, introducing proprietary Nu Sans Display and Nu Sans Text typefaces, and establishing a global library of photography, illustration, and motion assets. The system also extends into conversational AI, in-app animations built with Rive, and a redesigned global website, bringing greater consistency to Nubank's growing international presence.

design.title: Is this the most controversial font since Comic Sans?
design.summary: AI-generated posters are becoming recognizable through their repeated use of aggressive, upward-slanting brushstroke lettering, prompting comparisons with the much-maligned Comic Sans. ChatGPT attributes the repeated aesthetic to training data that associates oversized, distressed lettering with dramatic, attention-grabbing advertising and promotional graphics. Unlike Comic Sans, which was designed for a specific communication purpose, the AI-generated lettering often imitates expressive typography without understanding its context, turning a once-distinctive style into a visual cliché.

design.title: Design Feedback for AI Agents
design.summary: Design systems and agent instructions can guide AI-generated interfaces toward consistency, but they cannot anticipate every combination of components, layouts, and product states. A lightweight feedback loop helps close the remaining gap by letting designers annotate screenshots, comment in Figma, or provide spoken and written instructions that agents use to correct visual problems. Intent now integrates this workflow through a macOS screen-feedback feature, while human judgment remains essential for deciding which corrections should become reusable design system rules.

design.title: What does design system AI readiness mean, anyway?
design.summary: Making a design system AI-ready requires more than machine-readable documentation, design tokens, MCP servers, and agent skills. AI agents need constraints that guide them toward approved components, patterns, and implementation rules while reducing opportunities for inconsistent or invented solutions. The real measure of readiness is whether AI can participate in the design process without lowering quality, with human judgment remaining essential wherever tacit knowledge and context cannot be fully encoded.

design.title: Visual Handoff for Humans and Agents
design.summary: A macOS menu bar app for visual handoff. Freeze or record your screen, annotate with gestures, and hand the finished session to a human or a coding agent.

design.title: Build a Polished Website or Web App with AI
design.summary: Describe what you want to build. Modulify turns your prompt into a polished landing page, website, dashboard, or app, ready to edit, refine, and launch.

design.title: Free Online Image Dithering Tool
design.summary: Free online image dithering tool. Floyd-Steinberg, Atkinson, Bayer ordered dithering, animated GIFs, and multi-image upload — processed locally in your browser.

design.title: “Designing a Good Poster is a Dark Art” – Highlights from This Year's INTL Poster Competition
design.summary: This year's INTL poster competition drew 2,670 entries from 78 countries, with 190 posters by more than 200 designers on display in Glasgow from November 12–22. Co-founder James Gilchrist calls a great poster near-impossible to design and singles out three trends: layered surfaces, 1990s-inspired collaged typography, and deliberately unprofessional, playful work.

design.title: Superior Type's Heaven is a sans serif built on oversized round shapes
design.summary: Superior Type's Heaven is a brutalist grotesque designed by Petr Kucera around oversized rounded shapes that appear compressed into rectangular spaces. The typeface includes four families, Heaven 01, 03, 06, and 09, each offering 18 styles from Thin to Black with italics, Latin and Cyrillic support, and a SuperVariable version that transitions from soft, rounded forms to boxier geometry. Distinctive curved letterforms, unconventional diagonals, and optional alternates give designers flexibility for expressive logos and display typography while retaining enough balance for longer text.

design.title: Designing a better future: your guide to design contribution in Open Source
design.summary: Open-source projects often lack the UX expertise needed to make powerful software approachable, while designers struggle to discover contribution opportunities in developer-oriented environments such as GitHub. Meaningful contributions can include user research, clearer project descriptions, onboarding improvements, navigation, error messages, accessibility, and better documentation of design processes rather than just visual assets. Designers can begin by exploring projects they already use, reviewing contribution guidelines, finding relevant issues, and collaborating directly with maintainers, even without extensive technical knowledge.

design.title: Apple reports Q4 2026 earnings: $114.5 billion in revenue, up 12%
design.summary: Apple reported record September-quarter revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12% year over year, and $30.71 billion in net profit.

design.title: German Artist Paints Luminous, Dreamlike Worlds That Feel like a Warm Sigh of Relief for the Soul
design.summary: German artist Vin Clovercreek paints journeys of friendship and wanderlust in twilight pinks, soft purples, and warm glows, setting lone figures against vast landscapes.

design.title: Figma Adds Version History for AI Plugins and Shaders
design.summary: Every edit now saves a new version with an agent-generated description, while earlier ones stay available to review and restore.

What hasn't changed is why clients hire you: your expertise, backed by numbers they trust. 79% of agencies save 5+ hours a week with AI, according to 494 agency professionals AgencyAnalytics surveyed this year. marketing.title: AI traffic drives 83% more revenue per visit
marketing.summary: Adobe found that AI-referred traffic generated 83% more revenue per visit and converted 90% better than non-AI traffic in September. AI visitors also spent 73% more time on site and added products to carts 53% more often. However, the average retail homepage scored just 63% on Adobe's AI readability measure. Product specifications, setup guides, and customer service pages were easier for AI to understand.

marketing.title: Companies may need to restrict AI use to manage costs
marketing.summary: OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, and Meta are spending billions on AI development but struggling to turn their investments into profits. OpenAI reported more than $20B in operating losses in the first half of 2026, while Anthropic's infrastructure costs have surged 329% year over year. xAI has already restricted Grok access because of high operating costs. AI companies may introduce tighter usage limits to control spending as pressure to deliver returns grows.

marketing.title: Let's get the first 100 users for a startup
marketing.summary: Many of the best early-user channels work because they're too small for bigger companies to chase. Smaller podcasts are often short on guests and open to founders who demo the product on air. Newsletters under 10K subscribers cost a few hundred dollars to sponsor and often beat larger ones on ROI. Buying a tiny app with an overlapping audience for $1K to $10K gives a ready base of users to redirect.

marketing.title: “Why did you cancel?” email
marketing.summary: Set up an automated cancellation email that asks customers why they canceled their subscription. Send it immediately and keep it short and conversational to encourage honest feedback. Use their responses to identify improvements or start conversations that could win back former customers. An example is provided in the post.

marketing.title: How to identify LinkedIn Ad visitors
marketing.summary: Use LinkedIn Sales Navigator's Smart Links to identify people visiting your landing page before you reach the 300-person minimum for retargeting audiences. Create a Smart Link for your landing page and use it in your Thought Leader Ads. Sales Navigator will show visitors' names, companies, and job titles. Then reach out directly to understand why they didn't convert.

marketing.summary: Flightcast lets creators automatically distribute their existing YouTube video catalogs to Spotify for $100/month. Creators can connect their YouTube accounts and transfer individual videos, playlists, or entire catalogs, with future uploads syndicated automatically. Flightcast also adapts titles, descriptions, and chapters for Spotify.

marketing.title: Why PR is the New SEO (Thanks to AI) (40 minute podcast)
marketing.summary: AI is bringing SEO and PR closer together as brands compete for visibility beyond website clicks. Amanda Milligan from Semrush explains why earned media and third-party mentions influence AI visibility. She also shares how Semrush builds its B2B YouTube strategy by balancing search-driven videos with content designed for YouTube's recommendation algorithm.

marketing.title: How Text Overlays in Social Media Images Affect Engagement
marketing.summary: Large or centered text overlays lower engagement when the image underneath is dynamic. A busy image already draws the eye, so big central text creates a competing focal point that makes the post look disorganized. Static images can carry larger, centered text, which guides attention instead of fighting for it.

marketing.title: Audience analysis for CRM and email: how to understand people well enough to send the right message at the right time
marketing.summary: Effective CRM marketing starts with understanding what people need when you contact them, not just who they are or what triggered an email. Track opt-in type and relationship stage in your CRM to distinguish intentional subscribers from people who signed up for a download or were added to a list. Analyze customer motivations and emotions around key triggers, collect the language they use to describe their needs, and review their email history to spot irrelevant or repetitive messages. Turn these insights into CRM properties and workflow rules that inform messaging at every stage of the relationship. Measure success through engagement by opt-in type, conversions by intent level, and fewer emails per conversion.

founders.title: Who Wins the AI App Layer?
founders.summary: AI labs are now shipping products aimed right at vertical AI customers, like OpenAI's tool for lawyers that launched a week after Harvey raised at $15.5B. Most of the value still lands with the apps, as long as they own data the labs can't simulate or buy. Coding took off because the labs can grade it automatically, so the moat is outcome data that only exists when someone does the job, like whether a loan defaulted or a claim got approved. A quick test is to list every outcome your product touches and capture the job byproducts as structured data from day one.

founders.title: 2026: The State of Enterprise AI
founders.summary: The labs selling you model access are also competing for your customers' software budgets. Menlo's yearly enterprise AI report estimates the frontier labs now capture 69% of enterprise AI deployment spending. Agents are growing the pie, though, since new budgets funded 55% of the extra AI spend in Menlo's survey, and the firm reads that as companies paying for work software couldn't do before. Startups still take 61% of application spending once the labs' own apps are left out.

founders.title: Analytics has changed. Here's what to do about it
founders.summary: Software stopped having near-zero marginal costs once AI features started showing up on the bill. Analytics has to change now that agents both run the analysis and use the product. Agents now create about half of PostHog's dashboards and feature flags, so the team tags every event with whether a human or an agent did it. The same tagging shows a third of orgs query PostHog through agents, and 1 in 5 new orgs signs up through one.

founders.title: How to make friends before fundraising
founders.summary: Most founders start meeting investors the week they start raising, so every coffee turns into a pitch. A former YC partner explains how to build those relationships months ahead so the eventual raise is fast and competitive. The list is bigger than founders think, since more than 4,700 Series A rounds since 2023 were led by about 2,400 different funds. One tactic is to script every intro ("we're not raising, and I want to meet you because of the company you backed") so the meeting doesn't accidentally start a process.

founders.title: Presenting an Annual Plan (AI-Era Edition)
founders.summary: AI can make an annual plan look leaner before any of the savings show up. The fix is to put AI spend right beside the headcount plan and show when avoided hires or extra output will hit the numbers. Revenue needs the same split, because usage-based AI products can carry very different margins from the subscriptions next to them. Give the AI cost of free trials and proofs of concept its own line too.

founders.summary: Claude Enterprise-managed auth is an authorization and authentication model for connectors in Claude. It allows administrators to provision connector access centrally instead of having every person authenticate each connector individually. Administrators can control which connectors are enabled, which groups or roles get them, and at what access level. Teams get connectors automatically the first time they log in once they are enabled for an organization.

founders.title: Introducing: Email Assistant by Superhuman Mail
founders.summary: Superhuman Mail Email Assistant brings the best of Superhuman Mail directly into Gmail and Outlook. It separates what needs a reply from what is just an FYI, resurfaces important conversations, and archives low-priority emails. Email Assistant can draft replies in users' voice and tone using context from other emails and information from online research. Users remain in control of how Email Assistant writes, schedules, and triages.

founders.title: The SaaS apocalypse started in October
founders.summary: AI-built competitors are the easy explanation for any SaaS slowdown this fall. Stripe benchmarks covering about 181,000 subscription businesses show 29 of 48 groups above $100,000 ARR shrinking in October, up from four in September. Customer churn went down over the same stretch, leading the writer to suspect weaker new sales. Only companies above $5 million ARR were still growing in October.

founders.title: Who Owns the Intelligence Economy?
founders.summary: An AI that learns from your best salesperson can keep using their methods after they leave. Companies need to decide who owns that expertise before model providers end up controlling it. Keep workflows portable between providers so switching models doesn't wipe out what the company's AI has learned.

crypto.title: Kim Jong-Un's sister rejects North Korean links to $6B Binance hack
crypto.summary: Kim Yo-jong, a senior North Korean official, rejected the FBI's assessment, saying the FBI is trying to brand the country a “cyber criminal state.” Three firms, including TRM Labs, and the FBI over the weekend attributed the hack to North Korean actors. TRM says the attacker tested code on three wallets, then used EIP-7702 to turn a Binance hot wallet into a sweeper, with 50 pre-signed authorizations so one would stay valid. Earlier Monday, Binance published its first proof of reserves and said it replenished about 95% of affected assets with its own funds.

crypto.title: $146M Drained From Two Exchanges in 24 Hours Extends Four-Day Hack Streak
crypto.summary: Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest centralized exchange, lost $40M in an exploit on November 2, while an unnamed EU-based exchange lost $106M the same day, bringing the combined single-day custodial loss to approximately $146M. Both incidents fall within a four-day window that also includes what market observers are calling the largest exploit on record, raising questions about a coordinated attack vector or shared infrastructure vulnerability across venues. The cluster puts renewed pressure on CEX hot wallet exposure and cross-jurisdictional key management practices.

crypto.title: Introducing Silver: Gattaca's New Ethereum Consensus Client
crypto.summary: Silver is an open-source Ethereum consensus client built from scratch. It recorded median block-processing latency of 6.5ms (5.2x faster than next-best) and p99 of 9.5ms (9.6x faster) across 20,300 canonical mainnet blocks benchmarked against Prysm, Lighthouse, and Grandine from October 17-20. The performance gains stem from Gattaca's thread-per-core, share-nothing Flux runtime with six CPU-pinned tiles, a new p2p layer supporting up to 2 Gbit/s gossip traffic, and a formally verified BLS/KZG crypto library delivering 2x+ throughput over existing implementations. Gattaca's roadmap targets EIP-8198 (Quick Slots for shorter slot times) and EIP-8292 (post-quantum attestation), with plans to publish the underlying libraries so other client teams can adopt them. Silver is currently in alpha, with audits and final testing still pending.

crypto.title: Consensys launches cross-ledger settlement and routing stack
crypto.summary: Launched at Devcon in Mumbai, “Sovereign Network Interoperability” lets banks settle across independently run blockchains without moving assets off their native ledgers. It covers securities settlement, collateral mobility, wholesale and cross-currency payments, and funds servicing. A Cross Ledger Interoperability Protocol built on zero-knowledge research verifies cross-ledger state cryptographically, with no bridges. An institution sets its requirements and approved counterparties, and the software picks a route, coordinates execution, and tracks the result. EVM networks are supported now, with Canton planned, and it will also support the Ethereum Economic Zone standard and IBC. The launch follows Consensys' October 8 ClearToken partnership and September split of MetaMask from its institutional business.

crypto.title: The Balance of Power
crypto.summary: Stripe's Link Balance converts user deposits to USDC on its Tempo chain, holds them in Privy non-custodial wallets, and liquidates back to a Lead Bank virtual card at checkout, letting merchants receive a standard Visa payment while Stripe accumulates stablecoin float. The three-step roadmap moves from card-funded to bank-transfer-funded balances, then to Stripe's Machine Payments Protocol, which routes consumer-to-merchant flows on Tempo with no Visa involvement, no interchange, and instant settlement. With 350M Link users, $1.9T in annual merchant volume, and a free open stack of Tempo (rails), OUSD via Bridge (money), and MPP (protocol), Stripe is commoditizing each payments layer while concentrating network effects at the wallet. Autonomous agents route to whatever rails are cheapest. Stripe is now using this against Visa interchange, but future entrants could apply the same logic against Stripe's own network moat.

crypto.title: The Next Front in the Personal Agent Wars: Consumer Finance
crypto.summary: Dedicated finance AI agents will displace general competitors like Meta's Muse and Instinct for money management, because their incentives run in opposite directions: general agents monetize via transaction fees and advertising, rewarding spending, while finance agents succeed when users save more. Licensing and fiduciary obligations compound the divide, as general agents lack the compliance infrastructure to move money, recommend investments, or manage debt. Crypto rails resolve the infrastructure gap: agent-owned wallets interact with any protocol without logins, programmable conditions enforce user limits at the wallet layer, and stablecoin settlement runs 24/7 with every action auditable on-chain. The projected end state pairs a life-concierge general agent with a finance CFO agent coordinating via agent-to-agent messaging, with US stablecoin legislation now providing a regulated on-chain rail from launch.

crypto.title: Agentic products are getting ahead of themselves on access
crypto.summary: Teams are racing to give agents access through virtual cards, API credentials, prepaid balances, and tokens without addressing what happens once they're inside. The harder problem is whether an LLM understands what a person asked for (intent), what the system allows (execution), and whether the two match. A payment can clear and still be the wrong purchase, and access doesn't equal authorization, which doesn't equal intent. Cards and API wrappers won't solve the problem, so teams need to understand the whole transaction lifecycle. AI makes software easier to generate but not easier to architect, and infrastructure has to be deliberate.

crypto.title: Coinbase Q3 Earnings
crypto.summary: Coinbase posted Q3 GAAP net income of $719M, but adjusted net income came in at $78M after stripping out $641M in unrealized gains on crypto held as a treasury asset. CFO Alesia Haas confirmed the GAAP figure reflects mark-to-market appreciation, not operational earnings. Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong filed a 10b5-1 plan to sell up to 8.17M COIN shares (~$1.31B) through October 2027, with co-founder Fred Ehrsam and COO Emilie Choi entering similar plans for up to 3.87M and 1.56M shares. The pre-scheduled filings insulate executives from insider trading claims and represent a combined potential disposal of over 13.6M shares.

crypto.title: Why agent payments are stuck
crypto.summary: Intent has no standard shape, nothing checks an agent before it pays, consumers don't trust agents (60% quit after one mistake), merchant fraud tools are built for humans, issuers approve blind, there are no cross-network liability rules, raw card vaults are a PCI gray area, agent tokens barely work (Chase won't provision), virtual card fronting is expensive and networks dislike it, and agents still can't monetize.

crypto.title: Binance completes latest proof of reserves to verify user balances
crypto.summary: Binance completed a zero-knowledge proof of reserves covering BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC, so users can verify balances are backed 1:1.

crypto.summary: AERO has a $502.94M market cap, and holders receive $87.88M a year, which is 5.7x holder returns.

it.summary: AI agents are joining the workforce, but the security policies aren't keeping up. Research from JumpCloud found that 59% of organizations using AI agents haven't fully integrated them into the identity policies used for employees. That's a problem as agents increasingly access applications, execute tasks, and make decisions. With JumpCloud's Agentic IAM capabilities, IT teams can discover agents, establish ownership, manage permissions, and govern access throughout their lifecycle, alongside human and device identities. Because as the workforce evolves, security needs to evolve with it. Secure every identity. Human or not.

it.title: Snowflake previews AI agents that work after you log off
it.summary: Snowflake announced CoCo and CoWork Bots, agents in development that will handle ongoing tasks in the background and request human input when needed. Separate updates add recurring automations and planned integrations with Slack, spreadsheets, and mobile devices.

it.title: Suspected cyberattacks spoil food at European supermarkets
it.summary: More than 40 supermarkets across seven countries were affected by suspected attacks that remotely raised refrigeration temperatures, destroying food. The incidents highlight the exposure of connected operational equipment that can remain in service long after its software support ends.

it.title: Is AI saving time or making work longer?
it.summary: ActivTrak's latest research associates heavy AI use with longer workdays, shorter focus sessions, and more app switching, contradicting some of its earlier findings. Different samples and measurement limitations make the results difficult to compare, underscoring why usage metrics alone cannot establish productivity gains.

it.title: Rushed AI layoffs could lead to costly rehiring
it.summary: Gartner predicts that 30% of employees replaced by AI will be rehired by 2029, likely at a higher cost. The firm argues that companies should assess how work needs to change before deciding which roles to cut.

it.summary: Bull and Schwarz Digits signed an agreement to develop AI infrastructure for European organizations in regulated and strategic sectors. The planned architecture combines STACKIT's European cloud with Bull's computing hardware, liquid cooling, and AI software.

it.title: Snowflake adds centralized controls for enterprise AI agents
it.summary: Snowflake's generally available Cortex AI Gateway centralizes policies for agent connections, model access, and spending. Its upcoming Business Ontology preview will give agents approved definitions of business concepts, while sandbox execution and agent-abuse detection remain in private preview.

it.title: National Grid plans major substation for data center expansion
it.summary: National Grid plans a major substation at Teesside to support a proposed data center, battery storage, and other power-intensive industries. Its initial 1,440 MVA capacity is scheduled to come online by the end of 2029, illustrating the long infrastructure timelines behind AI expansion.

it.title: CIO survey exposes the gap between AI rollout and readiness
it.summary: Accenture's survey of 300 technology leaders finds 64% are scaling enterprise AI deployment, but only 7% are optimizing it at scale. User adoption and training are the most frequently cited execution barrier, while nearly half still require manual approvals for agents in IT operations.

it.title: UK businesses face looming digital phone migration deadline
it.summary: Openreach warns that roughly 300,000 business copper lines remain active ahead of the January deadline, including connections supporting payment terminals, alarms, and building systems.

it.title: AI agents fuel projected 55% growth in identity spending
it.summary: Juniper Research forecasts global identity and access management spending will rise from $26.2 billion in 2026 to $40.5 billion by 2031 as businesses manage expanding populations of AI agents and other nonhuman identities.

hardware.title: SpaceX's Starfall is a flat disk capsule built to return up to 1,000 kg from orbit
hardware.summary: Starfall is an uncrewed SpaceX reentry capsule shaped like a disk, about 10 feet across and 2.5 feet tall, that launches on Falcon 9, with Starship planned. It returns up to 1,000 kg from orbit by parachute and ocean splashdown, targeting about 700 nautical miles off the US West Coast. SpaceX's stated goals are fast point-to-point cargo delivery and return of in-space manufactured goods. The first demo launched on June 23, and it puts SpaceX in competition with return-capsule startups like Varda.

hardware.title: Apple warns memory costs keep rising, as supplier purchase commitments jump $33B in one quarter
hardware.summary: On its earnings call, Apple CEO John Ternus called memory pricing “unprecedented” and said costs will rise again in the December quarter and beyond. Apple's manufacturing purchase obligations rose $33 billion in the September quarter, to $89.7 billion, to lock in supply. It guided December gross margin to 45% to 46%, and expects Macs and iPads to stay supply-constrained through the holidays. Apple raised prices on some Macs, iPads, and iPhones earlier this year.

hardware.title: Qualcomm says HBC silicon passes lab validation: 18x LPDDR5X bandwidth, 5x HBM4 bandwidth per watt
hardware.summary: Qualcomm's first High Bandwidth Compute silicon passed lab validation. HBC bonds stacked LPDDR memory to an AI accelerator base die, so compute sits under the memory and data travels less. Qualcomm claims 18x the effective bandwidth of LPDDR5X and over 5x the bandwidth per watt of HBM4, from early tests. HBC debuts in the Dragonfly AI250 inference accelerator, sampling in the first half of 2027.

hardware.title: Foxconn plans to contract-build other companies' quantum computers, treating them as accelerators next to CPUs and GPUs
hardware.summary: Foxconn wants to turn other companies' quantum designs into production systems, without owning the qubit technology itself. Chairman Young Liu told CNBC he sees the machines as accelerators attached to CPUs and GPUs for hard NP-type problems, not general-purpose computers, and puts commercial viability at least two years out. One cost driver he flagged is cabling: a single cable built for the low-temperature requirements can cost over $1,000.

hardware.title: Orbital Matter prints a half-meter rigid beam in orbit by UV-curing extruded resin
hardware.summary: Orbital Matter's Replicator-2 satellite 3D printed a half-meter rigid beam in orbit by extruding coils of resin cured with UV light, a first for a free-flying spacecraft. One of two printers meant to deploy a solar array failed, but the boom the other made did deploy the array. Boom length is limited only by onboard resin, and the company thinks 100 m is feasible. A 2028 mission targets a 5 kW array, then 100+ kW per wing by 2030.

hardware.title: Intel's 14A PDK 0.9 goes to outside customers, with PDK 1.0 due in Q1 2027
hardware.summary: Intel released 14A PDK 0.9 to outside customers, with PDK 1.0 planned for Q1 2027. A PDK is the set of design rules and transistor models chip designers build against, so 0.9 is where external designs can start taking shape. Intel's schedule still has risk production for its own products in the second half of 2027 and volume production in 2028, and it claims 14A is ahead of 18A on defect density and transistor performance at the same stage.

hardware.title: Northwood Space raises $375M at a $2B valuation to scale satellite communications gear
hardware.summary: Northwood Space raised a $375 million Series C at a $2 billion valuation, co-led by a16z and DFJ Growth, alongside a financing agreement with HSBC. Founded in 2022 and led by CEO Bridgit Mendler, it builds antennas and software that help satellites communicate with Earth. It raised a $100 million Series B in January and won a nearly $50 million Space Force contract to upgrade the satellite control network.

hardware.title: Agility lists at roughly 1,550x 2025 sales with a -151% gross margin, while Unitree's humanoid margin premium shrinks
hardware.summary: Agility goes public via SPAC at roughly $2.8 billion on $1.8 million of 2025 revenue. Its gross margin was -151%, since a Digit costs about $125,000 to build against a $75,000 target. Unitree is worth about $40 billion on $239 million of revenue and 5,500 humanoids sold, but its gross margin slipped to 54%, and humanoids' margin edge over its other products shrank to 6 points. Agility spends about 4.5x Unitree's R&D on 1/134th of its revenue.
